3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that on getting possession in the shop of plot No. 1110 from the then possessor Rafizal Hoque Bepari he started grocery shop on 10.1.1964. Subsequently, while running the business of books in the name of Al-Amin Library, he entered into a contract to purchase the suit properties including the huts and building thereon with Advocate Birendra Nath Sen Gupta, a lawyer of Bhola Bar Association, the constituted Attorney of Chuni Lal Sen Gupta and others, the original owners of the suit properties. The Attorney received Tk.4,000/- on 15.5.1967 as an advance out of the total consideration of Tk.50,000/- and executed an agreement in favour of the plaintiff. As the plaintiff was given delivery of possession of the suit properties he was not worried because of the delay caused for various reasons in execution and registration of the deed of sale. Moreover, the plaintiff has been living there with his family and carrying on business in the suit properties for more than 12 years by paying municipal taxes. The then S.D.O. and CO. (Rev), Bhola claimed the suit properties in Miscellaneous Case No. 2(S.A.)/63-64 under section 92(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The constituted Attorney of the original owners filed Title Suit No.496 of 1963 renumbered as Title Suit No. 54 of 1988 in the 1st Court of the then Munsif, Bhola, which was decreed on 30.12.1978 declaring all the proceedings of the Miscellaneous Case as illegal and without jurisdiction. When defendant No. 1 tried to lease out the suit properties claiming the same as khas the plaintiff filed a petition for taking lease of the same just to avoid the imminent threat of being evicted. He filed Title Suit No. 358 of 1976 for permanent injunction and obtained an ad-interim order of injunction. When the said order of injunction was vacated, the plaintiff preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 169 of 1976 and obtained an order of stay. When the said Miscellaneous Appeal was dismissed on 31.8.1981, the defendants conspired to evict the plaintiff from the suit properties and as such, the plaintiff was constrained to file the instant suit. 

 4. Defendant No. 3 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. His case, in short, is that the suit is not maintainable as framed. The suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It is barred by limitation. It is bad for defect of parties. The further case of this defendant is that Chuni Lal Sen and others, the original owners of the suit properties, left for India in 1950 without disposing of the suit properties as a result of which there was none to pay the rent of the same. As such, the suit properties were sold in auction on account of non-payment of rent. In auction, the suit properties were sold to defendant No. 1 on 30.10.1963 and sale was duly confirmed on 30.12.1963. Accordingly, the suit properties became the khash land of khatian No. 1 of the government. Subsequently, suit plot Nos. 1109, 1115, 1111 were leased out to different persons in Settlement Case No. 142 BH/63-64 and those lessees had been possessing the same. Masuma Khatoon Girls' High School has been running in suit plot No. 1102 contiguous to suit plot No. 1103. This defendant got settlement of the entire land of suit plot No.1103 in two instalments. Defendant No. 3 constructed a semi pucca but on the leased land and had since been in possession thereof. The plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 358 of 1976 in the Court of Munsif for permanent injunction in respect of the suit properties but the suit was dismissed on 11.8.1984. There are one temple and a building in the suit plot No. 1103 and Nanibala Datta had been living in that building as a licensee under the original owner. When she left the building during the War of Liberation in 1971, the plaintiff illegally entered into the building by breaking open the lock and continued his illegal possession in the building of suit plot No.1103. To legalise his unlawful possession, the plaintiff collusively created an antedated agreement claiming the suit properties by forging the signature of deceased Birendra Nath Sen Gupta who left the country for India before 15.5.67 and died there. On 28.6.1982, the plaintiff was evicted from his unlawful possession of the suit properties. The plaintiff filed a petition for getting lease of the suit properties before the appropriate authority on different occasions admitting the suit properties to be the khas land of the government. Title Appeal No. 15 of 1979 preferred by the government was allowed on contest setting aside the decree passed in favour of the plain-tiff in Title Suit No. 54 of 1968. Subsequently, the defendant was given lease of the entire land of suit plot No. 1103 permanently. For the reasons stated, the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed with costs.
